BEGIN: Think about where our story began.
ONE_PERSON: One person entered a password and pressed Login.
FOLLOWED: We followed that request through the Phone, Gateway, Load Balancer, Auth Service and User Database.
AUTH_STATE: We discovered how a successful authentication becomes trusted state.
BOTTLENECK: But the system could not complete every Login because one shared database had reached its limit.
PROTECTED: We learned how to protect that database.
CAPACITY: But protecting a bottleneck did not give us more capacity.
CHOICES: So we explored new architectural choices.
REPLICATION: Replication gave us more places to serve suitable reads.
CONSISTENCY: Consistency rules helped us understand when those reads were safe.
SHARDING: Sharding showed us how separate database owners could distribute the work that replicas could not remove.
FAILOVER: And failover reminded us that capacity is only one part of reliability.
RESPONSIBILITY: Every improvement came with another responsibility.
MORE_COPIES: More copies required clearer consistency rules.
MORE_OWNERS: More owners required stronger coordination and recovery.
SYSTEM_DESIGN: That is the real work of System Design.
NOT_COMPONENTS: Not choosing the architecture with the most components.
TRADEOFF: But understanding which responsibility belongs where, which trade-offs we accept, and what happens when part of the system stops behaving as expected.
HUMAN: And behind all those decisions is still the same person.
LOGIN: Someone pressing Login and expecting the system to work.
SUCCESS: The architecture succeeds when the human journey succeeds
